correctness.rationale: Geometric fixed points are barycentric combinations constant on each entire group orbit; orbit simplices triangulate their fixed locus. Each orbit O_(a,u) has diameter 2; for q≥3 there is δ∈Z/q distinct from 0 and a−b, giving cross-orbit maximum exactly 2+d_H(u,v). Therefore the orbit complex is the q-vertex-clique blowup of the smaller flag Rips complex; each clone (a,u) has the same closed neighborhood and is dominated by (0,u). Projection/section simplicial contiguity commutes with r-inclusions, giving natural integral persistence isomorphisms, not just isolated Betti ranks. Explicitly checked q=3,n=2: three orbit vertices form a 3-clique; q=3,n=4: 27 orbit vertices and 27 edges at r=2, grouped into nine disjoint triangles; q=4,n=3: 16 orbit vertices; q=2,n=3: four orbit vertices form C4 at r=2, demonstrating sharpness.
